summary: Enryo Inoue was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He later served as a researcher there and founded Toyo University, serving as lecturer and manager.

Ensho Kanakura was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Tohoku University and Rissho University, and as president of Miyagi University of Education.
Ensho Kobayashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Hanazono University, where he is attested as a professor in 1988 and as professor emeritus in 2026.
Ensho Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University under doctoral supervisor Esho Mikogami. He was attested as a guest researcher at Ryukoku University in 2007.

Enshu Kurumiya is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD at Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong. He was attested as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1981 to 1985.
Entai Tomomatsu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University around 1917–1920. He held a post at Taisho University and founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya.

Erberto Lo Bue was a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London. He was a lecturer in Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan (around 1983–2004) and later worked at the University of Bologna.
Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Harvard University in 2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.
Eric Haruki Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who held a post at Loyola Marymount University and was attested as a senior visiting scholar at Stanford University in 2026.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Manchester and Uppsala University. He held posts at Lancaster, Uppsala, and the University of Sydney, where he was the first chair of religious studies.

Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He served as assistant professor and associate professor of religious studies at Yale University.

Eric P. Hamp was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Amherst College and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (around 1950–1953) and the University of Chicago (around 1953–1991).
Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner.

Erica Baffelli is a Japanology and religious studies scholar who studied under Massimo Raveri. She has held posts at the University of Otago and the University of Manchester, where she is attested as professor in Japanese studies in 2026.
Erica Biagetti is an Indology, linguistics, and computational linguistics scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Pavia by 2021 and held a post there.

Erich Frauwallner was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Vienna. He later served as director and professor of Indology at the University of Vienna and founded the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens.

Erich Haenisch was a sinologist, Iranian/Central Asian scholar, and Tibetologist who studied under Wilhelm Grube at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at the universities of Göttingen, Leipzig, Berlin, and Munich.

Erich Heintel was a philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served as an extraordinary and later ordinary professor of philosophy at the University of Vienna from 1952 to 1982.

Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a scholar of philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen and completed his habilitation at the University of Strasbourg. He served as an ordinary professor of philosophy at Halle-Wittenberg and Marburg.
